```plato

    //==
    // # Contact frames
    //
    // Friction acts in the plane of the contact, so every constraint row needs two
    // unit vectors spanning that plane. Any two will do geometrically; what
    // matters is that the SAME two are used for the life of the row, because the
    // accumulated friction impulse is stored in their coordinates.
    //
    // The tangent is built by crossing the normal with whichever cardinal axis it
    // leans on least, which is never degenerate: a unit vector cannot have a
    // component of magnitude one on two different axes.

    // A unit vector perpendicular to `normal`, chosen by crossing with the
    // cardinal axis the normal leans on least.
    Tangent(normal: Direction3D): Direction3D
    {
        var n = normal.Vector;
        var away = n.X.Abs <= n.Y.Abs && n.X.Abs <= n.Z.Abs
            ? Vector3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            : (n.Y.Abs <= n.Z.Abs ? Vector3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) : Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0));
        return n.Cross(away).Normalize.FromVectorUnchecked;
    }
```
